items.title: Fahmi calls for stronger cybersecurity, trusted AI adoption to drive Malaysia’s digital future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Industry players are encouraged to strengthen cybersecurity, promote responsible artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, share best practices and build trusted digital capabilities that would benefit Malaysia for years to come, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said as digital technologies become increasingly embedded across every sector of the economy, trust, security and resilience must advance in tandem with innovation. “As more organisations embrace digital technologies, trust will become just as important as innovation,” he said at the launch of U Mobile Enterprise Innovation Platform Hub here today.

items.title: Malaysia's wage structure needs review, says council
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's wage structure needs to be reviewed to ensure that workers earning above the minimum wage also benefit from periodic salary adjustments, said the National Wages Consultative Council. National Wages Consultative Council (MPGN) member Prof Emeritus Tan Sri Anuwar Ali said the government currently sets the minimum wage at RM1,700 per month. However, he said there was no clear mechanism to ensure workers earning RM1,800 or RM1,900 also receive salary increments.

items.title: Japan's Hiroshima marks 81st anniversary of atomic bombing
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's Hiroshima on Thursday marked the 81st anniversary of the United States (US) atomic bombing of the city amid growing concerns over nuclear risks and rising global tensions, reported Xinhua. During an annual memorial ceremony held at the Peace Memorial Park in the western Japanese city, Hiroshima Mayor Kazumi Matsui delivered the Peace Declaration, highlighting the catastrophic consequences of nuclear weapons and calling for nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament through multilateral efforts. Three days after the world's first-ever nuclear attack decimated Hiroshima, a second atomic bomb was dropped on Nagasaki in southwestern Japan.

items.title: Care home where man beaten to death found operating without valid licence
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said preliminary investigations revealed that the care home, which has been operating since 2012, only held a business registration with the Companies Commission of Malaysia. "The premises was also found to be without closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras," he said at a press conference after the rank-pinning ceremony for the Perak Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) chief and Taiping district police chief at the Perak Senior Police Officers' Mess here today. Alwi said the victim was one of 21 residents at the private care home.

items.title: Theta Edge shares hit six-month high on RM3bil Penang LRT contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of Theta Edge Bhd climbed to a six-month high after the company secured a RM3.028 billion railway systems contract for the Penang Light Rail Transit (LRT) Mutiara Line through a joint venture. The stock opened five sen, or 9.09 per cent, higher at 60 sen before surging as much as 17.5 sen, or 31.82 per cent, to 72.5 sen, its highest since Jan 22. Theta Edge, through its 10 per cent-owned joint venture with Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd (MRCB), has secured the RM3.028 billion system turnkey contract for the Penang Mutiara Line LRT project.

items.title: Q2 growth "should be okay": Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economic growth for the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026) "should be okay", Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said ahead of the official 2Q gross domestic product (GDP) announcement on Aug 14. The Statistics Department released its advance GDP estimates for Q2 2026 on July 17, which stated that Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.8 per cent, following the preceding quarter's growth of 5.4 per cent. Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.4 per cent in 1Q 2026, surpassing the advance estimate of 5.3 per cent.

items.title: Penang ranks third in international hotel guests, records nearly one million visitors in Q1 2026
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 6 — Penang ranked third in Malaysia for international hotel guests in the first quarter of 2026, recording 967,742 visitors, said state Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai. He said Penang was behind Selangor, which recorded 1,051,718 international hotel guests, and Kuala Lumpur with 3,006,280 guests. “Tourism has always been one of the key pillars of Penang’s economy,” he said.

items.title: Five senior officers promoted to key KL police leadership post
items.summary: Senior Assistant Commissioner (SAC) Sazalee Adam has been appointed the new Kuala Lumpur Criminal Investigation Department (CID) chief, replacing SAC Zulkarnain Samsudin, who has been appointed Selangor CID chief. Sazalee, the former Dang Wangi district police chief, was among five officers promoted from Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) to SAC rank. The other officers promoted are former Sentul district police chief Basri Sagoni, former Kuala Lumpur CID deputy chief (Intelligence/Operations) Zulkarnain, former Kuala Lumpur Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) chief Haslah Bachok, and Kamaruzaman Md Alib.

items.title: Pahang records over RM3m losses from telecom infrastructure vandalism, thefts
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 6 — Pahang continues to record a high number of vandalism and theft cases involving telecommunication infrastructure equipment, with total losses last year standing at over RM3 million. State Communications and Multimedia, Youth, Sports and Non-Governmental Organisation Committee chairman Datuk Fadzli Mohamad Kamal said the thefts, among others, led to communication disruptions in those areas, thereby affecting daily consumer affairs. He added that cables, batteries, communication equipment cards, diesel and Remote Radio Units are among the items stolen from communication infrastructure.

items.title: Five charged in Sabah over false Perkeso Daya Kerjaya 2.0 claims
items.summary: The accused are Pausia Abu, 49; Arzeanti Jafar, 40; Nur Farhanah Jamil, 38; Mohd Azhar Ramali, 39; and marketing executive Foo Fong Kent, 31. Foo faces three charges, while Pausia and Azhar each face two charges. Arzeanti and Nur Farhanah each face one charge.

items.title: KTMB: No timeline yet for reopening Kulai-Kempas Baru line
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Electric Train Service (ETS) operations between Kulai and Kempas Baru remain disrupted today as repair works continue following an accident that damaged the overhead electrification system. Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said there is still no timeline for the reopening of the affected section as crews continue removing a fallen concrete parapet that struck the overhead line equipment on both the northbound and southbound tracks. Three morning ETS departures from JB Sentral have been affected.

items.title: About 20,000 residents hit by foul odour, black water in Iskandar Puteri
items.summary: The pollution, affecting several housing estates along Jalan SILC 2/4, has raised fears of a public health and environmental crisis, with residents claiming the black, sludge-filled water eventually flows into Sungai Pulai and nearby rivers. Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad warned that failure to address the issue promptly could trigger a disaster similar to the 2019 Sungai Kim Kim toxic pollution incident. Pandak visited the site after receiving complaints from residents to assess the situation first-hand.

items.title: Tong Herr trading halted pending announcement, volume hits four-year high
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Trading in the shares of Tong Herr Resources Bhd was suspended this afternoon pending a material announcement by the company. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the trading halt took effect at 12.16pm. Headquartered in the Perai Free Industrial Zone, Tong Herr is listed on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia under the industrial products and services sector.

items.title: Warisan KL launches Xplorasi Warisan to rediscover Kuala Lumpur
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Warisan KL and its strategic partners will host Xplorasi Warisan KL: Edisi Merdeka on Aug 30, 2026, inviting Malaysians to rediscover Kuala Lumpur's heritage through a citywide adventure celebrating the spirit of independence. The heritage-based exploration will take participants through Kuala Lumpur's historic core, combining teamwork, discovery and interactive challenges across key landmarks within the Warisan KL heritage corridor. The explorace will take place alongside wider Merdeka celebrations at Warisan KL landmarks, including activities at Stadium Merdeka in the Merdeka 118 precinct and Ambang Merdeka festivities at Dataran Merdeka.

items.title: Malaysia’s services producer prices accelerate to 2.9pc growth in Q2 2026, says DOSM
items.summary: Accommodation and food and beverage services recorded the highest increase among the major subsectors, rising 6.4 per cent from a year earlier after growing 5.7 per cent in the previous quarter. Transportation was the second-fastest growing component, rising 5.6 per cent year-on-year compared with 3.8 per cent in the first quarter, largely due to a 17.5 per cent increase in passenger air transport prices. Real estate activities increased 0.6 per cent during the quarter, followed by education (0.5 per cent), health (0.3 per cent), information and communication (0.2 per cent) and professional services (0.1 per cent).

items.title: Four charged with submitting false documents for Daya Kerjaya 2.0 claims
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Four business owners were charged in the Sessions Court here today with a total of 30 counts of submitting false documents in Daya Kerjaya 2.0 incentive claims. Wong, the owner of JH Food Court, faced two charges allegedly committed on Aug 26, 2024. Neoh, meanwhile, faced 21 charges involving four different companies.

items.title: 19-year-old college student faces murder charge over stabbed newborn
items.summary: KLUANG: A 19-year-old female college student will be charged in the Magistrate's Court here tomorrow with the murder of her newborn baby. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said the decision was made after investigation papers were referred to the Johor deputy public prosecutor's office. "Based on the directive, the 19-year-old student will be charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code for allegedly murdering her newborn baby," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Penang Education Dept vows protection for student in cyberbullying case
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Education Department has assured protection for a student allegedly targeted in a sexual harassment and cyberbullying case that is currently under police investigation. In a statement today, the department said it was giving its full cooperation to police to facilitate investigations. "Psychosocial support interventions are being carried out to assist the affected student," it said.

items.title: Britons take drastic measures including sleeping in kitchen to cope with heat
items.summary: LONDON: One in six Britons are taking "drastic action" including sleeping in the kitchen, missing work or booking hotels, to cope with heatwaves, Citizens Advice has found, reported PA Media/dpa. The charity said millions across the United Kingdom (UK) are "trapped in homes they can't cool," with almost half (44 per cent) saying they lack basic control over keeping their homes from overheating. It is demanding government action on a "now year-round crisis" of "soaring heat in summer and unaffordable energy bills in winter."

items.title: PJ MP claims constituency funds routed through PKR division chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung has claimed that public funds allocated to the constituency are being channelled through a PKR division chief. Lee, whose access to the federal government's MyKhas portal was revoked in May, made the claim in a Facebook post today. The New Straits Times is withholding the division chief's name pending a response.

items.title: Toyo Tyre donates RM30k to Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Toyo Tyre Sales and Marketing Malaysia Sdn Bhd has launched its Community Prihatin Toyo initiative with a RM30,000 contribution to the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund, reinforcing its commitment to community welfare alongside business growth. The mock cheque was presented by Toyo Tyre Sales and Marketing Malaysia Sdn Bhd president and managing director, Tan Song Chye, to Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund representative Muhammad Nazim Ismail. Tan added that the initiative also reflects the company's newly unveiled brand identity, Buatan Malaysia, Keunggulan Jepun ("Made in Malaysia, Japanese Excellence"), which combines Malaysian manufacturing excellence with Japanese engineering standards.

items.title: Lorry driver charged with sexually assaulting two daughters in Seri Iskandar
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 6 — A lorry driver was charged in the Sessions Court here today with 21 counts of sexually assaulting his two biological daughters, aged 13 and 16, in Seri Iskandar. According to the charge sheets, he was accused of kissing the neck, touching and molesting the breasts and private parts of his 16-year-old daughter, as well as forcing her to perform oral sex on him. He was also accused of touching the private parts, molesting the breasts and rubbing the buttocks of his 13-year-old daughter, as well as forcing her to touch his private part.

items.title: Johor's call for more health workers is about service, not politics – Health Exco
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor rejected claims that its repeated calls for the federal government to urgently fill vacancies in state public hospitals were politically motivated. State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the appeal was solely aimed at ensuring better healthcare services for the people. Yesterday, Dr Rafidah Abdullah, a public health physician and prominent healthcare advocate urged Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi to go beyond calling on the Health Ministry whenever hospitals face staff shortages.

items.title: Zahid says those involved in TH mismanagement must face consequences
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 6 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Umno will not tolerate any breach of trust or mismanagement involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, said that anyone found involved in wrongdoing or mismanagement within government agencies and statutory bodies must be held accountable. A special parliamentary session to debate the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH will be held on Aug 11.

items.title: Former PH Rantau candidate, wife charged over unregistered clinic operation
items.summary: According to the first charge, the company was found to have operated a private medical clinic without registration under Section 27 of the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998. The company was charged under Section 4(1), which carries a maximum fine of RM500,000 upon conviction. For the second charge, the couple, in their capacity as company directors, were accused of jointly operating a private medical clinic without registration under Section 27 of the same Act.

items.title: New BMW iX3 heralds Neue Klasse era in Malaysia, priced at RM378,800
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The new BMW iX3 50 xDrive M Sport Pro has been unveiled in Malaysia, marking the debut of the brand's Neue Klasse electric vehicle (EV) portfolio here. The fully electric sports activity vehicle (SAV) comes with a recommended retail price of RM378,800. BMW Group Malaysia managing director Benjamin Nagel said the new iX3 represents the brand's most significant technological leap in a generation.

items.title: Selangor exco: Data centre growth not straining domestic water supply
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 6 — The demand for data centres in Selangor has so far not placed pressure on domestic water supply, particularly in densely populated areas, said state Investment, Trade and Mobility Committee chairman Ng Sze Han. He said the state government continues to emphasise sustainable data centre development that is balanced with environmental needs and the well-being of the people. “Air Selangor also continuously reviews future water requirements for data centres, with projected future demand estimated at 632MLD,” he said.

items.title: Looking past statistics on the retrenchment narrative
items.summary: LETTERS: A RECENT opinion piece warned that Malaysia's retrenchment wave has reached alarming, near-pandemic proportions, and that the government's claims of a healthy labour market ring hollow. The author stated that 52,607 workers had applied for unemployment benefits under Perkeso's Employment Insurance System (EIS) as of July 16, 2026, and Kuala Lumpur and Selangor together accounted for roughly six in 10 cases. It must be read together with DOSM's Labour Force Survey.

items.title: Fahmi backs U Mobile's innovation hub for enterprises
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has called on businesses to leverage U Mobile's Enterprise Innovation Platform Hub to strengthen cybersecurity and responsible artificial intelligence (AI) adoption. He said the hub showcases the practical applications of 5G-Advanced technology across industries, including healthcare, agriculture and retail. Fahmi said the technologies demonstrated could help ease nurses' workload in hospital wards, improve productivity at oil palm plantations, and enable retailers to manage inventory more efficiently while analysing customer traffic patterns.

items.title: Another suspected human skeleton found in gunny sack in Perlis, murder probe underway
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 6 — Police are investigating the discovery of another set of suspected human bones found protruding from a rotted white gunny sack in an overgrown area at Bohor Mali, near here. Kangar District Police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said police received a report from a 61-year-old man at 12.35 pm yesterday. Yusharifuddin said further investigations uncovered additional bones, along with a worn pair of boxer shorts, torn shorts and a belt.

items.title: BMW defends EV investment record in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: BMW Group Malaysia has defended its contribution to the country's electric vehicle (EV) ecosystem, saying its investments extend well beyond charging infrastructure to include talent development and technical capabilities. EV transformation and charging is one topic," said BMW Group Malaysia managing director Benjamin Nagel after launching a new BMW model here today. Transformation goes far beyond pure charging," he said.

items.title: BMW Malaysia urges balanced EV infrastructure push
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: BMW Group Malaysia calls for a balanced approach in expanding the country's electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure without placing unnecessary pressure on automakers. The company cautioned that any new measures should support EV growth without creating additional burdens for automakers. Managing director Benjamin Nagel said policy proposals should be discussed with industry players before deciding on the most effective measures to support Malaysia's EV transition.

items.title: Perkeso 24-hour protection claims surge more than threefold in July [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Claims under the Social Security Organisation's (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam scheme more than tripled in July, underscoring growing demand for round-the-clock social protection beyond working hours. Perkeso said claims jumped to 2,135 in July from 616 in the previous month, reflecting the relevance of the scheme, which extends coverage for work contributors outside official working hours. The payments covered medical expense reimbursement, temporary disablement benefits, funeral benefits, dependants' benefits, rehabilitation equipment and implants, as well as other forms of assistance.

items.title: Pahang orders immediate action on hazardous trees after deadly Janda Baik incident
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 6 — The Pahang government has directed all relevant agencies to hold immediate discussions to address the issue of hazardous trees following the tree-fall incident that claimed four lives in Janda Baik, Bentong, last Tuesday. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the discussions were aimed at coordinating action and identifying other high-risk locations to enable preventive measures to be taken to avoid similar incidents in the future. Wan Rosdy said trees identified as posing a risk would be assessed before appropriate action was taken, including felling them if necessary.

items.title: Amir Hamzah: Govt to unlock markets, private capital must drive investment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — The government’s role is to maintain a credible policy and fiscal framework while using public capital to unlock markets, enabling private capital to play a larger role in driving investment, Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said. He said that while the government can provide policy certainty and maintain a credible fiscal framework, financing innovation and business expansion must increasingly be undertaken by banks, institutional investors, venture capital firms and private equity players. Amir Hamzah said venture capital could take the earliest risks, growth capital and private equity could finance expansion, banks would play a bigger role as companies’ cash flows strengthened, and public markets would provide another source of capital as companies matured.

items.title: [UPDATED] Police expand AI, drones in border security push
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are stepping up the use of drones, artificial intelligence (AI) and cross-border intelligence sharing as part of efforts to combat smuggling and strengthen security along Malaysia's land and maritime borders. He said similar cooperation was also being carried out with Indonesian authorities along the Malaysia-Indonesia border. "We are using drones, enhancing intelligence sharing and looking at expanding technological capabilities, including AI, to strengthen border surveillance and enforcement," he said.

items.title: Abdul El-Sayed: Michigan doctor who wants to lead the left to the US Senate
items.summary: THE left-wing Democratic upstart set to contest a critical US Senate seat in November's mid-term elections is a charismatic 41-year-old who once said he would have been a cab driver in Egypt but for an "accident of history." Abdul El-Sayed on Wednesday sealed the Democratic Party's nomination to run for a seat representing the state of Michigan in the US Senate, beating out centrist candidate Haley Stevens who was backed by the party's top brass. "I got to go to amazing public schools, an incredible public university.

items.title: Missing couple and son detained in Kubang Pasu over alleged RM25,000 ‘kutu’ scam
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 6 — A husband and wife, previously reported missing together with their nine-year-old son, have been detained for allegedly operating a fraudulent ‘kutu’ scheme. Kubang Pasu police chief Supt Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the couple, aged 36 and 39, surrendered at the Kubang Pasu district police headquarters at about 1.30 am today. Police had previously confirmed receiving a report on the disappearance of a family of three, including their nine-year-old son, which went viral on social media recently.

items.title: [UPDATED] Police seize RM15.5m worth of vapes, contraband cigarettes in Selangor raids
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have seized contraband cigarettes and vape products worth more than RM15.5 million in two major operations targeting smuggling syndicates in Selangor late last month. Federal Internal Security and Public Order Department director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the seizures were made under Op Taring Alpha 1 and Op Taring Alpha 3. "Op Taring Alpha 3, conducted on July 28, targeted a premises in Batu Caves believed to have been used to store and distribute vape products.

items.title: I-Berhad's first half profit rises on recurring income, AI strategy growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: I-Berhad posted a higher pre-tax profit (PBT) for the first half of its 2026 (1H FY26) financial year, supported by stronger contributions from its property development and investment businesses, as it presses ahead with its artificial intelligence (AI)-driven urban development strategy. The company said 2026 marks a key milestone in its transformation from a traditional property developer into an integrated AI-enabled urban ecosystem, anchored by its AI Living and AI World initiatives. I-Berhad chairman Tan Sri Lim Kim Hong said the company's strategy is centred on creating a diversified earnings base by combining recurring investment income with AI-enabled developments.

items.title: Shell approves Malikai Phase 3 to lift Sabah oil output by 60pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Shell has approved the third phase of its Malikai deepwater development offshore Sabah. Siti Sulaiman, country chair of Shell Malaysia and senior vice president Upstream Malaysia, said the investment underscores Shell's long-term commitment to the country. Shell said the investment reflects its continued confidence in Malaysia's deepwater potential.

items.title: After Johor and Negeri Sembilan wins, Zahid sees ‘blue wave’ heading to Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 6 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said a “blue wave” could extend beyond Johor and Negeri Sembilan and soon reach Putrajaya, following Barisan Nasional’s (BN) strong showing in the two state elections. “The blue wave will continue. From Johor to Negeri Sembilan, and God willing, arrive here.

items.title: Zahid claims ministry officers ‘pressured’ over attending BN-linked events during state polls
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 6 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today alleged that some officers from his ministry had been “pressured” by “top people” in the government for attending events linked to Barisan Nasional (BN) during campaigning for the recent state elections. However, Zahid said his ministry’s officers were present only as part of their official duties. Zahid is BN chairman and Umno president.

items.title: MRT Corp awards RM3.03b Penang Mutiara LRT systems contract to MRCB-Theta Edge JV
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 6 — MRT Corp has awarded a RM3.028 billion system turnkey contract for the Penang Mutiara LRT Line, marking the project’s next major phase in the construction of Penang’s first Light Rail Transit (LRT) system. “The appointment will enable detailed design of the railway systems to proceed in parallel with the ongoing civil construction programme, ensuring both components remain aligned towards overall project delivery,” said MRT Corp in a statement today. MRT Corp said the Penang Mutiara LRT Line has continued to make steady progress through a series of key delivery milestones covering engineering design, construction planning, land readiness and railway systems implementation.

items.title: Johor MB launches Semarak Maghrib and Isyak programme to boost mosque attendance
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 6 — The Johor government has introduced the Semarak Maghrib and Isyak programme to be implemented at mosques across the state as part of efforts to strengthen the culture of congregational prayers, enliven mosques and foster syiar Islam (the propagation of Islamic values and teachings). Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the programme reflected the state government’s commitment to ensuring that mosques continued to serve as centres of worship, knowledge dissemination, and the strengthening of ukhuwah (brotherhood) among Muslims. He said the initiative was also among the Barisan Nasional manifesto pledges for the 16th Johor state election and would be implemented to fulfil the mandate entrusted by the people.

items.title: C4 calls for clearer mandate, transparency in MACC-Customs dept task force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Malaysia needs stronger transparency and accountability mechanisms to ensure government agencies can be effectively scrutinised by the public, said the Centre to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4 Center). He was commenting on the proposed special task force between the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) to address revenue leakages at ports. The anti-corruption watchdog said efforts to strengthen enforcement should also be supported by wider institutional reforms to improve transparency and accountability within government agencies.

items.title: Three Sarawakians arrested in Thailand with 87kg of syabu, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have confirmed that the three Malaysians arrested by Thai authorities with 87 kilogrammes of crystal methamphetamine (syabu) in Hat Yai are from Sarawak. He said Thai railway authorities detained the suspects in Hat Yai after discovering the drugs concealed in their luggage and backpacks. “Thai police and the Office of the Narcotics Control Board (ONCB) have shared preliminary details of the arrest with us.

items.title: Mohamad Hasan meets UN resident coordinator to discuss Malaysia-UN cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan received a courtesy call from United Nations Resident Coordinator (UNRC) for Malaysia Nikolas Myint at Wisma Putra yesterday. In a Facebook post, Mohamad said the meeting provided an opportunity for both sides to exchange views on cooperation between Malaysia and the United Nations. Myint was appointed as the UNRC for Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei by the United Nations Secretary-General on May 31, 2026.

items.title: Six-year-old autistic boy drowns after being swept away by waves at Kerteh beach
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 6 — An autistic boy was found drowned after being swept away by waves while at the edge of Pantai Kuala Kerteh near here yesterday afternoon. Kerteh Fire and Rescue Station Operations Commander Senior Fire Officer II Mokhtar Dollah said the victim, Muhammad Syahmi Farhan Mohd Firdaus, 6, from Kerteh near here, was found drowned by members of the public who also assisted in the search operation for the victim at 5:43 pm. He said the victim was found at a distance of 30 meters from the last location where he was seen playing with sand at the shoreline before being noticed missing.

items.title: KTMB services disrupted after lorry carrying flammable liquid causes power outage on Kulai-Kempas route
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 6 — The Shuttle Selatan and Electric Train Service (ETS) operations on the Kulai–Kempas route were disrupted yesterday following a power supply outage caused by a lorry carrying flammable liquid that skidded near the railway tracks. “For affected ETS passengers, shuttle bus services will be provided at Kulai, Kempas Baru, and JB Sentral stations. Fare adjustments will be provided to affected passengers,” it said.

items.title: Three Malaysian women held in Jakarta after drugs found hidden in luggage, shoes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Three Malaysian women were detained at the Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta on Monday in the latest drug-related case involving Malaysians abroad. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the police were informed by the Indonesian National Police (POLRI) about the arrest of the three women from Sabah, aged between 30 and 39. Hussein said the Royal Malaysia Police maintain a firm stance against cross-border crimes, with the NCID having seized 89 tonnes of various drugs nationwide last year.

items.title: Teacher found dead in SMK Bau toilet, police rule out foul play
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 6 — A female teacher was found dead in the toilet of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Bau yesterday morning. Bau district police chief Supt Mohd Haide A Rahman said police were alerted to the incident at about 8.53 am before a team was immediately dispatched to the school. Mohd Haide said the victim was last seen by a colleague in the teachers’ room at about 8.15 am, shortly before she went to the toilet.

items.title: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices down five sen this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel have each decreased by five sen per litre from Aug 6 to Aug 12, 2026. For unsubsidised diesel, the retail price is now set at RM4.57 per litre, compared with RM4.62 previously. Meanwhile, subsidised fuel prices remain unchanged, with Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) at RM1.99 per litre, Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) at RM2.10 per litre, the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) at RM2.05 per litre and the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) at RM2.15 per litre.

items.title: Bukit Aman to send team to Jakarta to probe Malaysian pilot drug case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will send a team of investigators and intelligence officers from Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (JSJN) to Jakarta, Indonesia next week to gather more information related to the syndicate network believed to be involved in a drug smuggling case involving a Malaysian pilot. Bukit Aman JSJN director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team will be in Jakarta from Aug 11 to 15 to assist in completing the investigation, including identifying the source of drug supplies, smuggling methods, and the possibility of the suspects’ connections with syndicates in Indonesia. He said the investigation is important to identify the entire distribution chain, including the possibility of involvement of other parties.

items.title: Anwar meets Singapore GP chief ahead of Formula 1 return to Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday met Singapore Grand Prix (GP) Executive Director Michael Roche ahead of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) this October. Formula 1 and the FIA previously announced that the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix will be held at SIC from Oct 2 to 4 under a collaboration between Malaysia and Bahrain. The Bahrain Grand Prix was originally scheduled to take place at the Bahrain International Circuit in April but was postponed to October following geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

items.title: Court declares Seremban-born girl a Malaysian, rules anti-statelessness protection applies to her
items.summary: The Court of Appeal has ruled that the answer is “yes”, holding that such a child has been “abandoned” as a newborn. They also do not know who her birth mother is. The Court of Appeal decided that a child is still considered abandoned when a birth mother permanently disappears after intentionally giving up the child to a responsible adult or safe person.

items.title: Cabinet congratulates Malaysian contingent on Glasgow 2026 success, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — The Cabinet today congratulated the Malaysian contingent for its outstanding achievement at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, said Madani Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. “The Cabinet took the opportunity to congratulate the Malaysian contingent at the Commonwealth Games, whose success has made the country proud and brought honour to Malaysia. The contingent surpassed the target of five gold medals and recorded Malaysia’s best performance at the Commonwealth Games since winning 12 gold medals at the New Delhi 2010 edition.

items.title: State and district education offices to nominate schools for MOE reform initiative, each to get RM100,000, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR, Aug 5 — District Education Offices (PPDs) and State Education Departments (JPNs) are responsible for identifying and nominating schools to participate in the Ministry of Education’s (MOE) school reform programme, Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said. He said 10 high-performing schools in each district, comprising five primary and five secondary schools, will be selected based on their academic achievement, co-curricular performance, and student character development. Announced on July 27, the school reform programme encompasses comprehensive improvements in school work processes, teaching methods, mental health support, and the overall well-being of the school community.

items.title: At 76, Mustapa Mohamed rules out GE16 return, urges young leaders to take helm
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Aug 5 — Former Jeli Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Mustapa Mohamed has reaffirmed that he has no intention of contesting in the 16th General Election (GE16), saying it is time for a new generation of leaders to take on greater responsibilities. Mustapa, who rejoined Umno in June through the party’s Rumah Bangsa initiative, said the country’s changing political landscape and evolving voter expectations make it important to provide opportunities for younger leaders. Mustapa left Umno in September 2018 to join Bersatu before rejoining the party in June this year under the Rumah Bangsa initiative.

items.title: Finance Ministry urges public not to spread false poster on RM100 SARA payout for National Day
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) today denied a viral claim that all Malaysians aged 18 and above will receive a one-off RM100 Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) payment in conjunction with National Day. In a social media post, MOF said the poster making the claim was false. The ministry advised the public not to believe or share the poster.
